text:
jordan: Heads-up — Signally (enterprise fintech) is evaluating a swap from CompetitorX to Redwood. They want a POC that keeps their current API surface via an adapter/transcode layer. Can we list the presales blockers and next steps?

sophia-se: quick checklist: 1) evaluate prompt parity (sample set), 2) confirm token billing diffs, 3) confirm auth + KMS + SIEM, 4) performance SLA and rate limits, 5) deploy plan for canary/fallback.

liam-eng: I can own the adapter shim proof-of-concept. Suggest we run a 2k prompt smoke harness comparing outputs (log-likelihood + embedding-similarity). Sample harness:
```bash
# run pairwise calls to CompetitorX and Redwood adapter
python tools/compare_responses.py --seed-file sig_prompts.csv --out diffs.json
```
Plan: run locally against staging adapter + collect token counts.

anika-security: Security Qs from Signally SQA: Do you support customer-managed KMS? Can we rotate keys? Full request/response audit logs? Data residency (EU)? Are there certifications (SOC2, ISO)? Need contact for pen test scheduling. Also: retention policy for prompt logs and redaction options.

mike-sales: Pricing/Q: They currently bill per-request with CompetitorX; Signally wants to understand per-token delta and a POC discount for 3mo Dedicated pool. Can we provide a rough TCO delta and a POC rate card? Also they asked about committed throughput for peak trading windows.

sophia-se: For prompt parity, propose an acceptance metric: >=0.88 cosine similarity on embeddings for top-1 responses OR manual review on 200 critical prompts. For behavior differences (function-calling/named entities) we'll include normalization layer in the adapter to map function signatures. Note: CompetitorX uses slightly different stop-token rules — include that in harness.

ci-bot: staging cluster "signal-compat-staging" provisioned in prod-sandbox-2 (nodes: g4dn x3).

liam-eng: Implementation notes: adapter will translate incoming request -> Redwood Generate API v2, attach client-id headers, and normalize responses back to CompetitorX schema. Edge cases: streaming vs non-streaming, chunked function-calls, role tokens in chat history. I'll add a small shim repo and ping for infra creds.

anika-security: To move forward we need: a filled security questionnaire (I can draft early answers), IP allowlist (customer will provide), third-party risk form, and contact for legal to sign DPA. If they require on-prem, we need network topology and approval matrix.

mike-sales: Timeline ask from customer: POC live in 3 weeks, 1-week smoke, decision in week 6. We should flag any blocker to hit that. Also they want an NDA + DPA signed before we run production-like tests.

sophia-se: Action items: 1) liam-eng: repo + harness by EOD tomorrow, 2) anika-security: draft SQ answers + DPA contacts by tomorrow noon, 3) mike-sales: capture pricing ask and initial POC discount proposal, 4) jordan: confirm the list of 200 critical prompts from customer. I'll own the parity evaluation and final acceptance script.

jordan: @liam-eng @anika-security @mike-sales thanks — please update this thread when your items are done. If we hit parity regressions we may need to propose a quantized fallback model to match latency/cost. Also flag any SLA gaps (99.9 vs their 99.95). :thumbsup:

ci-bot: new issue created: sales/POC-3512345678-adapter-transcode (assignee: liam-eng)

liam-eng: noted. I'll prototype the mapping and include token accounting to show delta per 1k calls. ETA for first commit: 48h.

sophia-se: Great. If anyone needs the prompt corpus, request it from Signally via @mike-sales and ask them to mark the 200-critical set.

jordan: ok — aiming for staging smoke in 3 weeks. I'll update the sales playbook and add a risk register in the deal doc.

mike-sales: pinging Signally to get the corpus and DPA contact now. Will update here.

anika-security: I'll start the SQ draft and share a link to the answers. If they need key-ownership, we can scope Redwood Private for the POC but that'll affect timelines.

sophia-se: tiny note — watch for response-format deltas when competitor returns multiple candidates in a single array. Adapter should collapse to single candidate by default to avoid client breaks.

jordan: thanks everyone — next sync if blockers appear.
